newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New HK legislature seen wasting no time post-handover.
newsitem.headline: New HK legislature seen wasting no time post-handover.

text.p: Hong Kong's shadow legislature may hold its first meeting on the territory's soil immediately after the British colony is handed over to China at midnight on June 30, government radio said on Thursday.

RTHK radio quoted Bruce Liu, a member of the council's working group on procedural matters, as saying the provisional legislature would meet in the early hours of July 1 to "confirm" laws drawn up before the handover but not yet enacted.
"There will be a debate, a short debate allowed for members, and it (the laws) would be confirmed and likely be at midnight after the handover," he said.

RTHK quoted him as saying the meeting would likely take place near the Hong Kong Convention Centre, where the official ceremony marking the handover will take place. Some 4,000 dignitaries are expected to attend the gala event.
Detailed arrangements would be decided next week when the provisional legislature holds its regular meeting in Shenzhen, just across the border from Hong Kong in China, the radio said.
Beijing will scrap Hong Kong's current elected Legislative Council (Legco) on grounds that the reforms that allowed the 1995 polls were illegitimate and enacted over its objections.

The shadow council, chosen by a China-backed committee of 400 selectors to replace Legco, has been meeting in Shenzhen to avoid having rival legislatures operating in the territory before the handover.
Controversy over its activities intensified this week when pro-China leaders said it could pass laws before the midnight handover.

Pro-democracy activists have said they would launch an immediate court challenge if the provisional legislature enacted laws before the handover. Hong Kong government officials believe a legal challenge would have some merit.
